NONE: › to remove the shell or natural covering from something that is eaten
剝…的殼；去…的外皮

example: to shuck corn/oysters
剝玉米／牡蠣

NONE: › to remove a piece of clothing, especially one that limits you
脫掉，脫去（衣物）
› to get rid of something that limits you or causes you problems
擺脫

example: The lifeguard shucked off his sweatshirt.
救生員脫掉了他的運動衫。
They seem to be able to just shuck off guilt.
他們似乎總能洗刷罪名。

NONE: › an expression of modesty, embarrassment, disappointment, or anger
（表示謙虛、尷尬、失望、後悔或厭煩等）唉

example: "You played great in the concert." "Shucks, everyone else was really good."
「你在音樂會上的表演很精彩。」「噢，其他每個人都演得非常好。」
Shucks, I missed the shot.
唉，我打飛了。
See also
aw shucks

NONE: C2 to shake suddenly with very small movements because of a very unpleasant thought or feeling
（因有令人不快的想法或感覺而）戰慄，發抖
› When something shudders, it shakes violently and quickly.
劇烈震動
› the act of shuddering
發抖，戰慄

example: The sight of so much blood made him shudder.
看到那麽多的血，他不禁渾身顫抖。
She shuddered at the thought of kissing him.
她一想到親吻他就禁不住發抖。
I heard a massive explosion and the ground shuddered beneath me.
我聽到一聲巨大的爆炸聲，腳下的地面隨之劇烈震動。
There was a screech of brakes and the bus shuddered to a halt (= shook violently and stopped).
伴隨著一聲尖厲的急煞車聲，公車劇烈地晃動著停了下來。
He gave a slight shudder as he considered how close he had come to death.
想到自己曾與死神那麽接近，他禁不住微微發抖。
She recalled with a shudder how her boss had once tried to kiss her.
她回想起她的老闆如何試圖強吻她時，不禁渾身顫抖。
figurative America's second biggest supermarket chain has sent a shudder through (= has had a strong effect on) its rivals by slashing its prices.
美國的第二大連鎖超市透過大幅降價給對手造成極大的震撼。

NONE: › If a system shudders to a halt, it suddenly stops working.
（系統）突然失靈

example: The economy has shuddered to a halt because of the civil war.
內戰使經濟一下子陷入停滯。

I + adv/prep, T: › [ I + adv/prep,  T ] to walk by pulling your feet slowly along the ground rather than lifting them
I usually + adv/prep, T: › [ I usually + adv/prep,  T ] to move your feet or bottom around, while staying in the same place, especially because you are uncomfortable, nervous, or embarrassed
（因不適、緊張或尷尬而）坐立不安，把腳動來動去

S: › [ S ] a way of walking in which you pull your feet slowly along the ground rather than lifting them

T: › [ T ] to move similar things from one position or place to another, often to give an appearance of activity when nothing useful is being done
把…搬來搬去；把…移來移去

C: › [ C ] the act of moving things around from one position to another
› [ C ] mainly US UK usually reshuffle an occasion when the positions of people or things within a particular group are changed

I or T: › [ I or T ] to mix a set of playing cards without seeing their values before beginning a game, so that their order is not known to any of the players

C: › [ C ] the act of mixing a set of playing cards before giving them out

U: › [ U ] a feature of an MP3 player, mobile phone, etc. that plays songs in a random order
（MP3播放機或手機等的）隨機播放功能

example: I love shuffling through the fallen leaves.
我喜歡在落葉上曳足而行。
He shuffled into the kitchen, leaning on his walking stick.
他拄著手杖拖著腳走進廚房。
Don't shuffle your feet like that! Walk normally.
不要那樣拖著腳走路！把腳抬起來。
The woman in front of me kept shuffling around in her seat all the way through the performance.
演出期間，我前面的那個女人在座位上不停地動來動去。
When I asked him where he'd been, he just looked at the ground and shuffled his feet.
我問他去了甚麽地方時，他只是看著地面，不停地擺動雙腳。
She shuffled her papers nervously on her desk.
她緊張地把桌上的文件移來移去。
Many prisoners have to be shuffled around police stations because of prison overcrowding.
因爲監獄過分擁擠，許多囚犯只得在警察局之間來回移轉。
It's your turn to shuffle the cards.
該你洗牌了。
She gave her papers a quick shuffle.
她迅速地把文件挪了一下位置。
We expect a Cabinet shuffle in the summer.
我們預計內閣將會在夏季進行重組。
Make sure you give the cards a good shuffle before you deal.
發牌前一定要好好洗洗牌。
I put my iPod on shuffle and drove home.
我開車回家，讓iPod隨機播放著歌曲。
a shuffle mode/function
隨機播放模式／功能
He's got arthritis and walks with a shuffle.
他得了關節炎，走路時拖著腳。

NONE: › to die
死，咽氣

example: My children can't wait for me to shuffle off this mortal coil so they can get their hands on their inheritance.
我的孩子們迫不及待地想我快些咽氣，這樣就能得到遺產了。

NONE: › to get rid of something unwanted, usually by giving it to someone else
（通常透過給予其他人而）擺脫；推開（不想要的東西）

example: Not until this turbulent region can shuffle off the burdens of the past will it be able to settle peacefully into the community of nations.
只有在這個動盪地區卸下其歷史重擔之後，才能和平地建立一個民族共同體。
The local authority may then try to shuffle these responsibilities off onto another authority.
這個地方部門可能想將這些責任推給另一個部門。

NONE: › to look at something quickly
瀏覽

example: Can I have a shufti at your paper?
我能瀏覽一下你的報紙嗎？

NONE: › to avoid something
避開，避免
› to ignore someone and not speak to that person because you cannot accept their behaviour, beliefs, etc.
躲避，迴避

example: She has shunned publicity since she retired from acting.
告別舞臺生涯後，她便遠離了大眾的注意。
After the trial he was shunned by friends and family alike.
審判後，朋友和家人都躲著他。

T: › [ T ] to move a train or carriage onto a different track in or near a station using a special railway engine designed for this purpose

T usually + adv/prep: › [ T usually + adv/prep ] to move someone or something from one place to another, usually because that person or thing is not wanted, and without considering any unpleasant effects

C: › a hole or passage that allows liquid to move from one part of the body to another, either found naturally in the body or put into the body in an operation
（身體不同部分之間自然或通過手術開啟的可讓液體流動）的通路

example: I spent most of my childhood being shunted (about) between my parents who had divorced when I was five.
我五歲時父母離異，童年的大部分時間都在離婚的父母之間輾轉。
He shunts his kids off to a camp every summer.
他每年夏天都送孩子們去參加夏令營。
Viewers are sick of their favourite sitcoms being shunted to later times to make way for live sports coverage.
因現場直播體育比賽而把深受觀眾喜愛的情景喜劇往後順延，許多人對此表示不滿。

NONE: › a small railway engine that is used for moving carriagesaround on the tracks rather than making journeys between stations
（鐵路的）轉轍器
› used to tell someone to be quiet
噓（要某人保持安靜）
› to (cause to) stop talking or making a noise
（使）停止喧鬧；（使）停止說話

example: Shush! I want to listen to the news.
噓！我要聽新聞。
I wish you kids would shush and let me read the paper in peace.
孩子們，我希望你們能安靜下來，讓我安安靜靜地看報紙。
He tried to shush the children.
他設法使孩子們安靜下來。

I or T: A2 to (cause to) stop operating or being in service, either temporarily or permanently

NONE: B1 closed
關閉的，關上的

example: Please shut the gate.
請關上大門。
I've got a surprise for you! Shut your eyes tightly and hold out your hand.
我要給你一個驚喜！緊緊閉上眼睛，伸出你的手。
Mary shut her book and put it down on the table.
瑪麗闔上書，把它放在桌子上。
This window won't shut - it's jammed.
窗戶關不起來——它卡住了。
The shops shut at eight o'clock on Wednesday evenings.
商店每週三晚上八點鍾打烊。
I suspected something was wrong when I noticed her curtains were still shut at lunchtime.
我發現午飯時間她的窗簾還拉著，就懷疑出了甚麽事。
figurative The government ought to have opened the door to Japanese investment instead of slamming it shut.
政府應該向日本的資金敞開大門而不是讓其吃閉門羹。
See also
open-and-shut

NONE: B2 to stop talking or making a noise, or to make someone do this
使（某人）閉嘴，使（某人）停止說話
› to stop someone from talking about a particular subject or from complaining or asking for things
使（某人）不再談論（某話題）；堵住（某人）的嘴巴

example: I wish you'd shut up for a moment and listen to what the rest of us have to say.
我希望你能閉上嘴巴安靜一會兒，聽聽我們其他人說甚麽。
Just shut up and get on with your work!
快閉上嘴巴繼續工作！
My dad never stops talking. It's impossible to shut him up!
我父親話一直說不停。讓他停下來簡直是不可能的！
figurative If you breathe a single word to the police, we'll shut you up for good (= kill you).
如果你向警察透露一個字，我們會讓你永遠閉上嘴。
The kids kept saying how hungry they were, so their father gave them some biscuits to shut them up.
孩子們總嚷嚷說自己餓了，於是他們的父親給了一些餅乾堵住他們的嘴。

NONE: B1 If a business or a large piece of equipment shuts down or someone shuts it down, it stops operating.
關閉；（使）停止運作

example: The company plans to shut down four factories and cut 10,000 jobs.
公司計劃關閉四個工廠，精簡一萬個工作名額。
The crew shut down the right-hand engine of the aircraft.
機組人員關閉了飛機右側的引擎。

NONE: › If a machine or system shuts off, or if someone or something shuts it off, it stops operating.
關機；關掉，關閉
› to stop the supply of something
關閉（或切斷）…的供應；停止供應
› to prevent something from being reached or seen
把…封閉起來；將…隔離

example: The engine shuts off automatically when the desired speed is reached.
達到設定的速度後，引擎會自動關閉。
Did you remember to shut off the water and gas before you left the house?
離開房子的時候，你記得關掉水和煤氣了嗎?
Oil supplies have been shut off.
燃油供應被切斷了。
The music room is shut off from the rest of the house by a soundproof wall.
隔音板把音樂間和屋內的其他房間隔開了。
A row of tall fir trees shuts off the view of the street in front.
一排高大的杉樹擋住了前面的街景。

NONE: › to close a shop or other business for a period of time, usually when business is finished for the day
關閉（商店等）；關門，打烊

example: By the time we got there, all the market traders were shutting up.
我們到那裡的時候，所有的店鋪都關門打烊了。

NONE: › to put a person in a place that they are not allowed or able to leave
把（某人）關起來，使（某人）與外界隔絕

example: He was ten years old when he was shut away for stealing an apple.
他十歲時因偷了一個蘋果而被關了起來。

NONE: › to prevent your opponent in a sports competition from scoring any points
不讓（對手）得分；以對方得零分的比分淘汰

example: She had shut out two of her first four opponents.
她淘汰了4名對陣選手，其中兩名沒有得一分。

NONE: › to prevent someone or something from leaving a place, usually by closing or fastening a door or gate
（為防止逃脫而）把…關起來，把…關在…裡

example: The cat was shut in the garage all night.
貓在車庫裡被關了一整夜。
He was so upset that he shut himself in his bedroom and refused to come out.
他難過得把自己關在臥室裡，不肯出來。

NONE: › to stop someone or something from entering or getting back inside a house or other building
阻止…進入，把…關在外面
› to not include a person or organization in an activity
把…排除在外

example: The wind blew the door closed behind me and now I'm shut out (of the house).
風在我身後把門關上了，現在我被關在了（房子的）外面。
Don't forget to shut the cat out when you leave for work.
出門上班時，不要忘記把貓關到門外。
Anna felt shut out of the conversation.
安娜覺得自己插不上話。
What are the chances of peace if we shut the terrorists out of negotiations?
如果將恐怖分子排除在談判之外，和平的可能性有多大呢？

NONE: › to keep a person or animal in a closed place
把…關起來，囚禁

example: She can't spend her whole life shut up in her office.
她不能一輩子都呆在辦公室裡不出來。

NONE: › to put something in a place where other people cannot see it or get it
隱藏，把…藏起來

example: The diamonds are shut away in a bank vault somewhere.
鑽石被藏在銀行保險庫的某個地方。

NONE: › to catch part of your body or an object inside a device or container when it closes
把…卡在…裡；把…夾在…中

example: Steve was off work for a week after he shut his hand in the car door.
史蒂夫的手被車門夾傷後，他一個星期沒有上班。

NONE: › to stop yourself thinking about something that upsets you or feeling something that hurts you
不再去想，停止想（不愉快的事情）
› to prevent a sound or light from being heard or seen
阻擋，阻隔（聲音或光）

example: She finds it impossible to shut out the memory of the accident.
她發現自己不可能忘記那次意外。
The double glazing shuts out most of the traffic noise.
雙層玻璃阻擋了大部分交通噪音。
She pulled the blankets over her head to try to shut out the light.
她拉起被子蒙住頭，試圖擋住光線。

NONE: › to end an activity, usually a business activity, either temporarily or permanently
歇業；關門；停業

example: Many companies are considering shutting up shop in this country and transferring production to low wage economies.
許多公司都在考慮結束在該國的業務，將生産轉向低工資國家。

NONE: › to ignore something
對…視而不見

example: Until now the prime minister has shut his eyes to the homelessness problem.
直到現在，首相仍對許多人無家可歸這問題視而不見。

NONE: › a rude and angry way of telling someone to stop talking
閉嘴，住嘴（粗魯且憤怒的說法）

example: He told me to shut my mouth or there'd be trouble.
他叫我住嘴，否則就會有麻煩。
"You're a lazy slob!" "You shut your mouth!" (= Don't talk to me like that!)
「你是個懶鬼！」 「閉嘴！」

NONE: › to go into a place that you are unwilling to leave and where you do not want to be interrupted by other people
把自己關起來

example: Andy shuts himself away in his studio for hours on end when he's recording a song.
安迪錄歌時會把自己關在錄音室達數小時。

NONE: › to stop speaking to other people or stop being involved with them
把自己封閉起來，不再和別人來往

example: When her husband died she seemed to shut herself off from her friends and family.
丈夫去世後，她似乎不再與她的朋友和家人來往了。

NONE: › to be so late in taking action to prevent something bad happening that the bad event has already happened
爲時已晚
› an occasion when a business or large piece of equipment stops operating, usually for a temporary period
（尤指暫時的）關閉；暫停運行

example: It's just a regular maintenance shutdown.
這只是一次定期保養停機。
The emergency shutdown procedure was activated.
緊急關閉程式啓動了。

NONE: › sleep
睡眠

example: You look exhausted! Try to get some shuteye on the train.
你看起來很疲憊！盡量在火車上睡一會兒吧。

NONE: › a situation in a sports competition in which a player or team wins without the other player or team scoring any points
輸方一分未得的比賽

C: › the part of a camera that opens temporarily to allow light to reach the film when a photograph is being taken
› a wooden cover on the outside of a window that prevents light or heat from going into a room or heat from leaving it
› a metal covering that protects the windows and entrance of a shop from thieves when it is closed

example: Shutters usually come in pairs and are hung like doors on hinges.
窗戶遮板通常是成對的，像門一樣掛在鉸鏈上。

C: C1 a vehicle or aircraft that travels regularly between two places
穿梭運行的車輛，接駁車;穿梭航班
› specialized fabrics in weaving, a device that is used to carry the thread that goes across the cloth between the threads that go down the cloth

NONE: › to travel or take people regularly between the same two places
往返穿梭；往返運送（人）

example: To get across town, you can take the shuttle from Times Square to Grand Central.
要穿越市區，你可以乘坐從時代廣場穿梭到中央車站的穿梭巴士。
The American (space) shuttle was able to be used many times to put payloads in space.
美國的太空梭可以多次使用，向太空運送物品。
A bus shuttles constantly between the terminal and the runways.
一輛公共汽車往返於機場大廳和跑道之間。

NONE: › discussions between two or more countries, in which someone travels between the different countries, talking to the governments involved, carrying messages, and suggesting ways of dealing with problems
穿梭外交
› a small, light object with a rounded end to which real or artificial feathers are fixed, that is hit over the net in the game of badminton
羽毛球
